scope.description: Complete functional offertory constituent within the native Præparationes ante Missam division, Paris 1606 printed p.181 right column (BSB canvas 235): from the red Offertorio dicto, eleuatis patena cum pane, & calice, & genufle. dicat. instruction through the final Amen of the Dominus sit response. Includes all three standalone red rubrics, the complete Suscipe Trinitas and In spiritu humilitatis prayers, the Orate invitation, printed red response cue and complete Dominus response. Offertory names a bounded function introduced by the source wording, not a separately printed chapter title. Creed above and in the left column, subsequent prefaces and all other book divisions remain outside this constituent. Whole-book and complete-Ordinary text coverage remain partial; no text is inherited from another edition.
omitted_book_divisions: The Creed above the opening instruction and in the left column of printed p.181
Other material of Præparationes ante Missam before the Offertorio dicto opening
The following prefaces, Canon, communion and all other Ordinary outside the stated bounds
Calendar, propers, lectionary, chant and all other missal divisions
Page furniture, running head, signature q, show-through and glyph-diplomatic typography

sources.transformation: Direct reading normalization of retained BSB canvas 235, printed p.181 right column: long s becomes s; display initials merge in sentence case; line-end word divisions and printed line wraps are joined within each semantic block; printed nasal suspension bars are expanded (including chorum, dicens, meum and sacrifícium); printed u/v, æ/œ, accents, abbreviations, punctuation and ampersands are retained. The stylized red crossed-R response cue followed by m. is represented as ℟m., without expanding the abbreviation. No absent Amen, prayer ending or familiar Roman wording is supplied. Six NFC UTF-8 physical lines, each a complete semantic block, end in LF. The Orate invitation and Dominus response retain their distinct source paragraph boundary. The spoken wording of those two blocks is byte-identical to the corresponding spans of existing checked orate-response-checked-latin-2bab0892; this broader source-derived selection restores the printed response cue omitted by that narrower spoken-only comparison. The separately bound Suscipe Trinitas reuses its existing checked passage unchanged. Rubrics are separate lines/units; their red ink, and red initials in the prayers, are recorded in the extent census rather than encoded as colour. This is a normalized reading transcription, not a glyph-diplomatic facsimile.

sources.transformation: Manual transcription of the exact retained image SHA-256 2646b0f5aa0a2bb55fd1042680a673e6adb99ec66913f754a8ceeac0f14830d7 at Cistercian missal 1606, printed p. 181, right column; BSB canvas 00235. Normalize long s to s; merge display initials with the following letters in sentence case; remove line wraps and line-end word division; expand printed nasal suspension bars; retain printed u/v, æ/œ, accents, B. abbreviations, punctuation and the 1657 (vel meis) alternative. Separate standalone and intervening red rubrics from the spoken body, recording their source positions below; omit response cue glyphs from spoken text. Preserve the 1657 inline alternative (vel meis), including its red vel, as printed textual evidence. Join spoken blocks with one space. Preserve the source’s actual short endings rather than expanding them from other editions. Write one NFC UTF-8 line followed by one LF. These disclosed reading conventions make this a normalized transcription, not a diplomatic reproduction. sources.title: Missale ad vsum sacri Ordinis Cisterciensis. Iuxta decreta Capituli Generalis dicti ordinis, Romano conformius redditum, primo accentibus ornatum & auctum

title: Cistercian 1606, Præparationes ante Missam: complete offertory constituent

units.source_locator: Paris 1606 Cistercian missal, printed p.181 right column; BSB canvas 235; normalized physical line 1.
units.text: Offertorio dicto, eleuatis patena cum pane, & calice, & genufle. dicat.

units.source_locator: Cistercian missal 1606, printed p. 181, right column; BSB canvas 00235.
units.text: Súscipe Sancta Trínitas vnus Deus hanc oblatiónem: quam tibi offérimus in memóriam beátæ passiónis, resurrectiónis, & ascensiónis Dómini nostri Iésu Christi, & in honórem beátæ Maríæ semper Vírginis genitrícis eiúsdem Dómini nostri, & ómnium Sanctórum & Sanctárum, cœléstium virtútum, & viuíficæ Crucis: vt eam acceptáre dignéris pro nobis peccatóribus, & pro animábus ómnium fidélium defunctórum. Qui viuis & regnas Deus. Per ómnia sǽcula.

units.source_locator: Paris 1606 Cistercian missal, printed p.181 right column; BSB canvas 235; normalized physical line 2.
units.text: Hanc sequentem orationem dicat Sacerdos incuruus ante altare post offerendam.

units.source_locator: Paris 1606 Cistercian missal, printed p.181 right column; BSB canvas 235; normalized physical line 3.
units.text: In spíritu humilitátis & in ánimo contríto suscipiámur, Dómine, à te, & sic fiat sacrifícium nostrum, vt à te suscipiátur hódie, & pláceat tibi Dómine Deus.

units.source_locator: Paris 1606 Cistercian missal, printed p.181 right column; BSB canvas 235; normalized physical line 4.
units.text: Postea erectus vertat se versus chorum dicens.

units.source_locator: Paris 1606 Cistercian missal, printed p.181 right column; BSB canvas 235; normalized physical line 5.
units.text: Oráte, fratres, pro me peccatóre: vt meum páriter ac vestrum in conspéctu Dómini acceptábile fiat sacrifícium.

units.source_locator: Paris 1606 Cistercian missal, printed p.181 right column; BSB canvas 235; normalized physical line 6.
units.text: ℟m. Dóminus sit in corde tuo & in lábiis tuis, suscipiátque de mánibus tuis sacrifícium istud: & oratiónes tuæ ascéndant in memóriam ante Deum pro nostra, & totíus pópuli salúte. Amen.
